doctrine: Complete operating system for Sniped Media built on three core principles: (1) Systematized Taste: Systems are repeatable; taste is abstract. Engineering rigor applied to visual direction (10-protocol Direction Stack diagnosing mechanical/psychological camera failures). (2) Psychological Environment: Studio as controlled machine lowering psychological defense mechanisms while elevating natural authority. (3) Cultural Gravity: Network node strategy—Eagle Rock studio as nexus where founders, artists, and operators converge. Revenue architecture: Tier 0 (Collab Free: 1 hero image + $250 gallery unlock), Tier 1 (Sprint: $275, 1hr), Tier 2 (Standard: $550, 2hrs, 10 images), Tier 3 (Reset: $1,500+, full Direction Stack deployment). Three free work categories: Collab Free (models/MUAs with audience), Community Free (local authority figures for cultural gravity), Access Free (events/promoters for status/proximity). LinkedIn as boardroom (visual systems for founders), Instagram as taste surface (editorial portraiture, no sales copy). VIB (Visual Infrastructure Board) as core outreach asset. Operator positioning separates from vendors: diagnose gaps, deploy systems, not take photos. Price justification rooted in risk mitigation and trust, not time/deliverables. Core metaphor: Engineering mindset applied to subjectivity. Field Engineer in data centers = rigorous systematization; photography = subjective creative work. Synthesis: engineer the certainty into the subjective.

operating_rules: Saturday = capture day only. Weeknights = editing, outreach, admin.
Send 3 VIBs/week minimum to LA founders on LinkedIn.
Deliver 1 hero image free; rest gated at $250 gallery unlock via Pixieset.

Clinical aesthetic non-negotiable: monochromatic, severe pose, skin as contrast point.
Never send >40 proof images to client; 150 is decision paralysis (Taste vs. Meal).
Culling: AI drops blinks/blur; manual selection <15 mins per 1-hour shoot.
Commerc licensing: If brand uses free collab photo, invoice $500-$1,500/image/year.
Retainer threshold: $1,500/month D2C retainers needed for studio rent coverage.
Direction Stack protocols 1-10 are the methodology; never delegated.
Base plate capture (studio lighting) never delegated; AI augmentation only on defined architecture.
No emoji, no hustle porn, no algorithm chasing on LinkedIn or IG.
Operator voice: diagnostic, understated, clinical. Never ask audience opinion on final product.

contradictions: Free work is encouraged as 'strategic acquisition' but also framed as dangerous 'free photographer trap'—resolved by strict gating (1 hero image only) and category separation (Collab/Community/Access)

Full Direction Stack deployment is the 'non-delegable' methodology, yet editing is delegated to Evoto AI batch processing—resolved by posture direction being on-set (human), retouching being post-production (system)

Operator positioning rejects 'creative' language, yet the entire business hinges on subjective taste/aesthetic judgment—resolved through framing: taste is intuition; systems are processes that amplify intuition consistently

LinkedIn should be 'business-facing' with no pricing visible, yet pricing tiers ($275/$550/$1,500) exist and should anchor value—resolved by showing high-ticket Reset first on internal pricing sheet, never public

Full ecosystem planning (Lion Group, Meridian, Wonderhouse) is presented as long-term vision, yet strict instruction is to focus only on Sniped Media for next 12 months—resolved: IP planning is mental vault, not active distraction
weird_gold: The tethered monitor as 'psychological weapon': subject sees premium output live, confidence spikes in real-time, changes posture for rest of session—not just technical tool but confidence engineering
The 48-hour Pixieset gallery expiration timer as mandatory scarcity: FOMO drives upsell, not sales pressure—system handles monetization automatically without awkward 'pay me' texts
VIB (Visual Infrastructure Board): undeniable visual diagnosis that forces conversation; stationary image (not animated) to avoid 'not-creepy test' that animated headshots fail
The 'Taste vs. Meal' architecture: free time/vibe in studio, gated final deliverables—flips typical freelancer model (all-inclusive) to premium model (curator gatekeeps)
Engineering background as ultimate differentiator: creatives perceived as chaotic, engineers as bulletproof—synthesis = systems that guarantee subjective outcomes
Studio as character/mythology more than location: overlapping clients in waiting area as intentional network broking; playlist/music/temperature as controlled environmental variables, not 'vibes'
Direction Stack as book (finished, private, held for authority) vs. LinkedIn protocol breakdowns (public intellectual distribution)—codification separates methodology from execution
The 'Quit Job' threshold as three simultaneous conditions met (1.5x salary, 6mo personal runway, 6mo business runway) prevents emotional exodus—data-driven escape velocity, not desperation
Community plays as reputation acquisition, not charity: shooting head coach who posts image builds his authority + your authority simultaneously (peer status transfer, not vendor extract)
Live event positioning: not 'event photographer' but 'editorial archivist documenting operational backend'—completely reframes the work and the network (shoots managers/execs, not crowd)
workflows: Weekly Operating Cadence: Monday (Pipeline Sweep + Referral Asks), Tuesday (VIB Creation + Founder Outreach), Wednesday (Content Batching), Thursday (Brand Pitch Sweep), Friday (Delivery + Studio Prep), Saturday (Capture Only), Sunday (System Audit)

Founder Reset Flow: Identify trigger event → Build VIB in Figma → Send 80-word DM + Static Board → 10-min Discovery Call → Deploy Direction Stack on-set → Tethered capture with live monitor → Cull to 40 images → Deliver 20, gate 20 at $250 upsell

Collab Free Shoot Flow: Pre-frame text (1 hero free, rest gated) → Tethered shooting on-set → Day 1 deliver hero + Pixieset link → Day 2 verify Collab tag + BTS post → Day 3 voice note referral ask → Day 14 check for brand repost → Commercial sweep if used

Post-Shoot Conversion Sequence: Day 0 (Tether anchor verbal), Day 1 (1 hero + gallery link), Day 2 (Social verification), Day 3 (Referral ask), Day 14 (Brand sweep), Day 30 (Repeat client pitch), Day 90 (Retainer proposal)
Content Batching: Sunday evening batch-write 3 LinkedIn posts (Pillar rotation: Visual-Operational Gap, Direction Stack, Operator Reality, Visual Audits). Schedule M/W/F. Prep 1-2 IG posts from BTS.
Backup Protocol: SD card ingestion → Active SSD backup (Copy 1) → Backblaze cloud sync overnight (Copy 2) → Only format card when cloud sync 100% confirmed → Check MD5 hashes if critical
Commercial Licensing Trigger: Brand reposts image from free shoot → Find brand manager on LinkedIn → Send invoice + licensing agreement → Clear usage terms for 12 months

Live Event Coverage: Day before (all-access credential confirmation) → Show day (arrive early, shoot VIPs/architecture/tension) → 10 AM next day (curated gallery delivered) → Monitor reposts → Day 14 (retainer proposal or artist licensing pitch)
prompts: When a potential client asks 'What are your rates?', respond: 'Depends on scope. To ensure I have the right infrastructure, grab 10 minutes on my calendar so I can baseline your visual gap.'

For founder outreach DM with VIB: 'Hey [Name], saw the recent press push. Your operational level is incredibly high, but your visual presence doesn't match it yet. I built this contrast board to show the gap. Worth a 10-min chat to fix it?'
For pricing conversation: 'The $1,500 Reset is infrastructure investment, not a photoshoot. A weak visual baseline creates micro-friction with investors. We eliminate that friction.'

For saying no to low-value work: 'My architecture is built for controlled, high-contrast environments and B2B operator portraits. Standard event coverage is outside scope. I can connect you with a run-and-gun shooter.'
For community visibility offer: '[Coach Name]. I'm documenting LA cultural pillars. Your program level is heavy. 30-minute studio portrait session, no cost. What day next week?'
For commercial licensing catch: 'Looks like [Brand] is using the asset I shot. Love to see it. Attached: standard licensing invoice for commercial usage. Who handles this?'
For gallery delivery: 'Baseline assets are in. Review the proof gallery, select your top [X] images. Once locked, I'll apply final clinical retouch. Expires in 48 hours.'
For contact/inquiry form: Never ask 'What's your vision?' Ask: 'Where is your visual presence failing your business?' (Diagnostic, not vague)
